:::{#exm-vector-p-norm-limit}
#### The $\ell_k$ norm approaches the maximum norm as $k$ grows

Take $\vx = (3, -4)$ and $\vy = (-1, 5)$ in $\reals^2$.
The code computes $\norm{\vx}_k$ for several values of $k$, including $k = \infty$ as the maximum,
and checks the triangle inequality for $\vx$ and $\vy$ at each of them.

```{r}
#| label: vector-p-norm-limit
#| code-fold: false
lk_norm <- function(x, k) {
  if (is.infinite(k)) max(abs(x)) else sum(abs(x)^k)^(1 / k)
}

x <- c(3, -4)
y <- c(-1, 5)
ks <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, Inf)
norms <- sapply(ks, function(k) lk_norm(x, k))
triangle <- sapply(
  ks,
  function(k) lk_norm(x + y, k) <= lk_norm(x, k) + lk_norm(y, k)
)
data.frame(k = ks, norm = norms, triangle_holds = triangle)
```

By part 1 of @thm-vector-p-norm, the $\ell_1$ norm `{r} norms[1]` equals
$\abs{3} + \abs{-4} = `{r} sum(abs(x))`$,
and the $\ell_2$ norm `{r} norms[2]` equals $\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2} = `{r} sqrt(sum(x^2))`$.
By part 2, the norms approach the maximum norm `{r} norms[length(ks)]`:
at $k = `{r} ks[length(ks) - 1]`$ the $\ell_k$ norm is within
`{r} format(norms[length(ks) - 1] - norms[length(ks)], digits = 2, scientific = FALSE)` of it.
By part 3, the triangle inequality holds at all `{r} sum(triangle)` of the `{r} length(ks)` values of $k$.

:::
